Argonne Venting and Flaring Research Team (2017). Analysis of Potential Opportunities to Reduce Venting and Flaring on the OCS. BSEE Venting and Flaring Research Study Report, prepared by Argonne National Laboratory for the Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement, January 2017. No report number, DOI or URL printed.

Locators: main report printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 10); Appendix II briefings cited as "App. II p.N" with their own printed numbering (PDF page = N + 140). Region: U.S. Gulf of Mexico OCS offshore platforms. Main file: Table 5 characteristics of the 17 gas capture technologies as two processes (new complex and retrofit capital cost), construction period, maintenance cost annualized to opex-fixed (formula); Table 6 flare emission factors converted to kg/GJ; Table 7 (p.60) break-even social cost of carbon as abatement-cost in USD per short ton CO2e ("over 1000" left blank and noted; options 10, 14, 15 have no numeric value and are omitted); Appendix II briefing costs (programming, static seals, ejector, completions, foaming agents, OOC flare retrofit 2-4 million, redundant compressor lower bounds), microturbine capacity and derived efficiency. _measures.csv: Table 5 gas capture estimates and the briefing example savings. _other-values.csv: vent emission factors, CBA constants, Table 2 vent/flare shares, flare pilot and threshold figures, pump ranges. Not loaded: OCS-wide and single-complex NPV results (Tables 8, 9), applicability factors (Table 7, p.51), volume statistics and forecasts (figures), Appendix I regulations. No vapour recovery unit, high-efficiency flare or enclosed combustor is characterized.

(1) No price year printed in Table 5 or the briefings; the CBA is in constant 2016 dollars (p.42), used for Table 5; briefings (dated Nov 2016) given publication year 2017.
